Parsing Delimited Files

The most efficient way to read a file separated by specific characters like - is using the .split() method combined with a context manager.

terminal The Solution

Hover code for details
parser.py 
def get_questions(filename):
    with open(filename, 'r') as f:
        # Read the entire file content into a string
        content = f.read()

    # Split by the '-' delimiter and clean up whitespace
    questions = [
        q.strip() 
        for q in content.split('-') 
        if q.strip()
    ]

    return questions

warning

The "Empty String" Trap

If your file ends with a delimiter (-), standard splitting creates an empty string at the end of your list. The if q.strip() filter in our list comprehension automatically removes these empty entries.

memory

Memory Considerations

The .read() method loads the entire file into memory. This is perfect for text files up to a few hundred MBs. For multi-gigabyte files, you would need a "streaming" approach, reading chunk by chunk.

cleaning_services

Why Strip?

Splitting by - often leaves newline characters (\n) attached to your text. The .strip() method removes leading/trailing whitespace, ensuring your data is clean.
